subject: stan memory usage increasing faster than expected

messages.author: 78c9353f20f51a7d
messages.subject: stan memory usage increasing faster than expected
parts:
Hi,
I'm seeing some strange behavior with stan's memory usage. I have a stan
model whose memory usage should increase linearly with the number of
data points. However, I find that memory usage seems to increase as
N^1.8. (To determine the exponent I generated simulated datasets of
varying sizes and monitored stan's memory usage.)

I have triple-checked the .stan file for my model and none of the
vectors or matrices should increase in size faster than O(N). I'm
wondering if perhaps I've missed something, or perhaps stan is doing
something behind the scenes that I don't know about that's causing
memory usage to increase nonlinearly.

At any rate, I'm attaching the .stan file that I'm using. I'm running
stan from the Linux command line.

Thanks in advance,
Daniel

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stan memory usage increasing faster than expected
parts:
Hi Daniel,

Thanks for taking the time to do some profiling on Stan. I'm going to try to keep the response short.

The underlying algorithm for Stan is the No-U-Turn sampler (NUTS), which is an extension to Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC). In order to use HMC, we need the gradient of the log probability function. That's what's being built in the Stan model. Stan is using (reverse-mode) automatic differentiation to calculate the gradients. It's the auto-diff that will scale memory out non-linearly.

The next reasonable question might be "is there a bound on memory usage?" and the short answer is no. Memory usage depends on the model you're building, the operations used on the parameters / derived parameters, vectorization, partially evaluated gradients, ...

When you hear about us talking about vectorized distributions, we're tackling two problems. The first is a consistency in the language so Stan is easier to use. The second problem we're addressing is partially evaluating gradients so we're not relying on auto-diff for the derivatives of known functions, such as pdfs of distributions. This reduces the memory footprint and increases speed.

A lot of this is covered in the preface of the manual. Hopefully that clears up some confusion.


Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stan memory usage increasing faster than expected
parts:
To be more specific, auto-dif takes time proportional to the size of the expression tree used to define the log probability.

Your model should be order O(B * N * n_conv) to calculate the log probability and gradient.

This is done every leapfrog step within Stan, and we need to keep some bookkeeping around that's based on the length of the Hamiltonian simulation (2 ** tree depth).  What is the tree depth being reported by NUTS?

Also, memory usage will go up during the application running, but never back down, because we don't free until the very end.  We could change that behavior if it winds up being too constraining.

- Bob
